hints: Focus on the p subshell only, and remember Hund's rule that electrons spread out singly before pairing.
Write the p configuration for F ($2p^5$) and Ga ($4p^1$) and count how many orbitals are left with a single electron.
Now test the negative ions like $C^-$ and $Si^-$ with $p^3$, they have three singly occupied orbitals, not one, so eliminate any pair containing them.
walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as one unpaired p electron**

Think of a p subshell as three boxes ($p_x$, $p_y$, $p_z$). We only count boxes with exactly one electron in them.

Rule to use:
$$p^1 = 1 \text{ unpaired}, \quad p^2 = 2 \text{ unpaired}, \quad p^3 = 3 \text{ unpaired}, \quad p^4 = 2 \text{ unpaired}, \quad p^5 = 1 \text{ unpaired}$$

**Check the promising pair, F and Ga**

F is atomic number 9, so its outer shell is $2s^2 2p^5$. That is one electron short of full, so two orbitals are full and one has a single electron.

Ga is atomic number 31, so its outer shell is $4s^2 4p^1$. That is just one electron in an empty p subshell.
$$\text{F}: [\text{He}]2s^2 2p^5 \rightarrow 1 \text{ unpaired p}$$
$$\text{Ga}: [\text{Ar}]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^1 \rightarrow 1 \text{ unpaired p}$$

**Eliminate the other pairs**

$C^-$ is $2p^3$ and $Si^-$ is $3p^3$. By Hund's rule all three p orbitals are singly occupied, so that is three unpaired p electrons, not one.

$Ti^+$ is $[\text{Ar}]3d^2 4s^1$. Its unpaired electrons are in d and s, so it has zero unpaired p electrons.
$$C: 2p^2 \rightarrow C^-: 2p^3 \rightarrow 3 \text{ unpaired}$$
$$Si: 3p^2 \rightarrow Si^-: 3p^3 \rightarrow 3 \text{ unpaired}$$

**Conclude the matching pair**

Only F and Ga both give exactly one singly occupied p orbital. So that pair is the answer.

options.A: Ar+ is $3p^5$ so it does have one unpaired p electron, but C- is $2p^3$. With three electrons in three p orbitals, Hund's rule gives three unpaired electrons, not one.
options.B: B is $2p^1$ so it does have one unpaired p electron, but Ti+ is $[Ar]3d^2 4s^1$. Its unpaired electrons are in 3d and 4s, so it has zero unpaired p electrons.
options.C: F is $2s^2 2p^5$ which has one hole, so one unpaired p electron. Ga is $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^1$ which has one electron in the p subshell, so one unpaired p electron. Both match.
options.D: Se- is $4p^5$ so it does have one unpaired p electron, but Si- is $3p^3$. Like C-, a $p^3$ configuration means three separate singly occupied orbitals, so three unpaired p electrons.
